name: Nicobarese
region: The Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal (India)
defining_innovation: The Austroasiatic languages of the Nicobar Islands, the family's only island branch, which developed verb-initial word order.

chapters.title: Island Languages
chapters.body:
The Nicobarese languages are spoken on the Nicobar Islands, far out in the Bay of Bengal between Myanmar and Sumatra. They are the only island branch of Austroasiatic. When and how their speakers crossed the sea is unknown, and some linguists see a closer link with the Aslian languages of the Malay Peninsula. Unlike most of the family they put the verb first in the clause.

The islands are a restricted area of India, and the languages have been studied relatively little. The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami devastated many Nicobarese communities and left them dispersed.

turning_points.title: Across the Bay of Bengal
turning_points.description: Austroasiatic speakers settle the Nicobar Islands. There is no firm date, and whether Nicobarese is most closely related to Aslian or forms an isolated branch is disputed.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul & Roger Blench. 2011. The Austroasiatic Urheimat: The southeastern riverine hypothesis. In Dynamics of Human Diversity, ed. N. J. Enfield. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.

turning_points.title: Car Nicobarese in writing
turning_points.description: Missionaries and island teachers establish a Latin-alphabet orthography for Car Nicobarese, the variety of the northernmost island, used in church and schools.

sources.citation: Jenny, Mathias & Paul Sidwell, eds. 2015. The Handbook of Austroasiatic Languages. Leiden: Brill.
